steps.title: Panes and widgets
steps.markdown:
A dashboard is built from **panes** and **widgets**.

- A pane is a resizable container on the board.
- A widget lives inside a pane and shows or controls data.
- You can add several widgets to the same pane later.

In this tour, you will create one pane and place a time plot widget inside it.

steps.title: From datasource to widget
steps.markdown:
A **datasource** produces values. A **widget** consumes those values.

For this v1 tutorial, the datasource is a hardware-free **Signal Generator**. The widget is a **Time Plot Widget** that will display one generated signal.

steps.title: Create a pane
steps.markdown: Click **Add pane** in the header to create your first workspace area.

steps.title: Create a Signal Generator datasource
steps.markdown: Open **Datasources**, click **ADD**, choose **Signal Generator**, give it any name, set **Refresh Every (ms)** to **100**, and click **ADD**.

steps.title: Add a time plot widget
steps.markdown: On your pane, click **Add widget**. If the widget picker is open, choose **Time Plot Widget**.

steps.title: Bind one signal to the plot
steps.markdown:
In the plot editor:

1. Set **Source** to your Signal Generator datasource.
2. Leave **Variable** on **Signal**.
3. Click **Add channel**.
4. Set **Y Min** to **-2** and **Y Max** to **2**.
5. Click **Save**.

The step completes once the plot has at least one bound series from the Signal Generator.

steps.title: Tutorial complete
steps.markdown:
You now have the basic dashboard flow:

- create a pane
- create a datasource
- add a widget
- bind data into that widget

Keep this tutorial tab open and experiment freely. Launching the tutorial again will open a fresh tab.
